A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NTK-Selector research despite the changed title and format. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices provide sufficient readable material for a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original fine-tuning results across eight tasks, kernel measurements, sensitivity analyses and empirical NTK regression comparisons.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds baseline comparisons, kernel diagnostics, ablations, overlap analysis and evaluations on four additional tasks.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same embedding pre-selection, warm-up, summed-output LoRA gradients, random projection, average NTK utility scoring and top-N selection. The new theoretical and experimental analyses do not establish a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix H.11 and Table 16 add agricultural irrigation QA (AgXQA), solar-cell QA (SCQA), open-ended climate QA (ClimaQA Freeform), and Kinyarwanda news classification (KINNEWS). These substantially extend domains, language coverage and answer formats beyond the retained eight tasks.

E2.justification: V2 adds Embedding and Gradient selection baselines to Table 1 for both backbones across all eight original tasks. These provide substantial direct comparisons against simpler similarity criteria; the original Base, Domain-Only, Random, DSIR, LESS and TSDS comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The original main training configuration remains. New protocols include DeepSeek-R1-1.5B and Hermes3-8B kernel diagnostics, IA3 and full fine-tuning, 50-epoch learning-rate/batch-size tests, and a 30-epoch domain-only control. Added tasks introduce F1, BERTScore and Rouge-L evaluations, while approximation checks introduce Spearman correlations.

E4.justification: Appendix H substantially expands validation through kernel stability tests, approximation and projection fidelity checks, compute-performance analysis, an approximately update-matched control, warm-up and selection-stage ablations, and a 3-gram overlap audit. V1's scaling studies and selected-sample case studies are retained.

E5.justification: V1 specifies a fixed projection seed but no repeated-run counts or variability estimates. V2 newly states that main results average three runs and reports means and standard deviations over three independent runs for kernel stability in Table 6. This disclosure does not establish an increased run count for retained results.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive baseline, diagnostic, ablation and additional-task results while retaining NTK-Selector's main Table 1 scores. Qwen3-8B's LESS FPB score changes from 30.3 to 60.3 and its average from 69.9 to 73.7; the discussion still quotes the old 49.8-point decline. The original Figure 2b scatterplot and approximately 6% cross-term statement are replaced by distribution and rank-correlation evidence.

T1.justification: New Appendix E connects the approximation to pseudo-NTK, decomposes output gradients, introduces isotropic readout and structured backbone assumptions, and presents an O_p(d^(-1/2) + sqrt(r)/d) relative-error argument. The original stability theorem, its proof, the kernel expansion and kernel-regression derivations remain.

C1.justification: V2 broadens high-level kernel-stability claims from LoRA fine-tuning to fine-tuning generally and explicitly claims an extension beyond earlier idealized NTK approximations. The central auxiliary-data selection contribution and headline benchmark gains remain, with stronger narrative emphasis on general-data domain adaptation.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations attributing gains to selection beyond extra updates, describing warm-up as a modest contribution, and explaining CoT's role in matching reasoning patterns. It also discusses stability under moderate training regimes, divergence at extreme learning rates, conditional theoretical assumptions, and the limited leakage evidence supplied by 3-gram overlap.

D1.justification: V2 adds an official repository link, implementation rules for the new baselines, and clarifications about shared initialization, shared CoT supervision and selection-only warm-up. It also documents float32 gradient storage and resource costs. The original LoRA hyperparameter table, hardware description and prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix E explicitly identifies the approximation as a rescaled version of Mohamadi and Sutherland's pseudo-NTK and positions the contribution as extending it to pretrained finite-width LLMs. New discussions substantially expand connections to Tensor Programs, neural and linguistic collapse, and Jacobian spectral research, alongside citations supporting new experiments.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and portions of the introduction and conclusion are rewritten. Appendix headings are reorganized, acknowledgements and an impact statement are added, and the standalone reproducibility statement and contents page disappear. The main section sequence and most retained technical prose remain stable.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main layout, redraws and relocates retained plots, expands Table 1, replaces Figure 2b, and adds Figures 6–8 and Tables 6–16. Existing prompt and case-study figures are resized and renumbered. The enlarged case-study figure on page 38 also loses its visible caption.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the unchanged method. Its approximately update-matched control reports 69.5 for domain-only training versus 76.6 for NTK-Selector (Table 12), addressing an important alternative explanation left open in v1. New baselines, component ablations, approximation checks, overlap analysis and broader task coverage further strengthen the evidence, while Appendix E clarifies assumptions and prior-work relationships. These gains outweigh reporting problems, notably the revised LESS score conflicting with the retained 49.8-point-drop discussion.
